ask: check desktop/badresearch. Now analyze this whole folder and whole skills first. I think maybe we should somehow make it simpler if it's needed, because I think it's a lot overcomplicated for now. And also, when we are using this research skill, sometimes a lot of things that does not work. For example, step-by-step skills — they're not working, and coding agents have to read them manually and not invoke it. So it's first error. And second, I think we should revamp it fully. So don't skimp... Because quality is a priority... make agents and coging agentic cli's SOTA at any kind of research... use ALL our channels, ALL our top sources, videos, podcasts, transcripts, articles, researches, guides, workflows, pipelines from goated people, engineers, researchers at top companies, startups, research labs. also use desktop/researchfms teardowns all at the same time via multiple agents per source. graphs are only similarity/intuintion

baseline.what: A plain Claude Code session with WebSearch/WebFetch and a demanding prompt.
baseline.measured: 17 minutes, 5,930 words, 35 sources actually fetched, explicit counter-case section, honest 'what I could not establish'. Beat badresearch's fast route 3-0 on three blind-judge lenses INCLUDING accretion. It also performed a real multi-hop correction the pipeline did not: took a vendor's published formula, applied it to that vendor's own table, found every row understated 10x, and propagated the correction until the vendor's headline conclusion flipped.
baseline.consequence: This baseline is the bar. Any slice whose capability the plain session already reaches is DELETED, not built. The slices below are exactly the deltas it provably cannot reach.

slices.capability: I type /research <question> in any project and get a cited answer that used MY local corpus — the 407 teardowns, 41 transcripts, 190 articles, 100 x-guides that no web agent can reach.
slices.check: Run it on a question whose answer exists ONLY in the local corpus AND is not spelled out in any lane recipe: 'Does iterative retrieval beat a single well-formed expansion, and what numbers back it?' (answer lives in researchfms/AGENTIC_SEARCH_SPEC.md; verified absent from skills/). PASS = the answer cites a real path:line that `sed -n` reproduces.
slices.unknown: Whether one skill file can carry route + gate + lane pointers in under 250 lines without regressing to the process-scaffolding shape that measured -8.4 to -27.4pp.
slices.shape: One SKILL.md + references/lanes/*.md read on demand. Anthropic's own contract: bundled files are level three, read as needed; 'when the SKILL.md file becomes unwieldy, split its content into separate files and reference them.'
slices.trap: The skill's description competes in a shared listing budget measured live at 40,139 chars across 109 skills. A dropped description reads as a skill that does not work — indistinguishable from the bug we just fixed.

CAVEAT: I authored the file and wrote its size/description assertions afterwards, so those two never went red first. The lane-reference assertion DID go red for the right reason (5 missing lane files) and is the honest check here.

rows.does: END TO END: /research on the corpus-only question returns an answer citing a reproducible teardown path:line
rows.evidence: passed — uncontaminated cold-use run by an agent that had never seen this session. Contamination check done by the agent itself: grep over ~/.claude/skills/research/ for the answer's specifics (adaptive-rag|IRCoT|68.8|39.80|oracle router) returns 0 hits; I re-ran it and confirm 0. It invoked Skill(research) cleanly, read local-corpus.md and web-live.md, reproduced the reachability probe digit-for-digit (407/41/190/67), ran `bad lane-local` as documented, and cited AGENTIC_SEARCH_SPEC.md:169 — which `sed -n '169p'` reproduces exactly. BEYOND THE CHECK: it then verified the corpus's own citations against the primary PDFs and found TWO defects in AGENTIC_SEARCH_SPEC.md that this session had repeated as fact. Asked whether the skill changed the outcome it said yes, concretely: without the frontier and contradiction rules the natural stopping point was 'found a pre-synthesized answer with citations, done', which would have shipped both defects.

slices.check_original: Run it on a question whose answer exists ONLY in the local corpus (e.g. 'what did ZS Associates conclude about multi-agent research pipelines, and what did they replace it with?' — that is in researchfms/teardowns, not on the open web in that form). PASS = the answer cites a real teardown file with a line number that `sed -n` can reproduce. FAIL-SHAPE = a plain Claude+WebSearch session cannot answer it at all, which is the point.
slices.check_revision_reason: The original check used the ZS Associates question, and I then had the lane-recipe agent use that SAME question as local-corpus.md's worked example — so the file handed the answer to the reader. The cold-use agent caught this itself and said part 1 was untestable in a blind sense. Revised BEFORE any row was flipped on it, not after a failure.

slices.capability: The loop asks a question it could only have asked after reading something — and refuses one it could have asked at the start.
slices.check: On one real run, count the queries issued after wave 1 that contain a term which first appeared in a FETCHED DOCUMENT rather than in the user's prompt or the initial decomposition. PASS = that count is > 0 and the run log names which frontier item each query hit. If it is zero, the owner's thesis is unimplemented and this slice did not ship, whatever the tests say.
slices.unknown: What a frontier item actually looks like when a real reader produces it — the gate already fails on long multi-token items, and nothing produces items yet.
slices.shape: Extract entities/quantities absent from the question after each read; every subsequent query must name one. Harness computes new-domain/new-entity deltas BEFORE the prompt is built so the stop is auditable even if the model lies.
slices.trap: Subset containment is order-insensitive and non-contiguous, so a long contradiction string is unnameable in practice while a common-word item can be named incidentally. The producer's item FORMAT decides whether the gate is real.
delete: the fixed step-1 decomposition that freezes the query set before any evidence exists
coverage-driven re-fetch against pre-declared atomic items

rows.does: a reader returns {findings, verbatim spans, reachability} and never reasoning
rows.evidence: passed — agents/research-reader.md installed to ~/.claude/agents/. Contract: returns findings + verbatim spans + a 4-state reachability outcome + frontier candidates; explicitly forbids conclusions, recommendations, paraphrase-as-quote and silent failure. It is also the frontier PRODUCER S2-2 needs.

rows.does: a producer extracts frontier items from a real fetched body
rows.evidence: passed — RED first (ImportError: extract_frontier_items). Producer emits entities, named methods, arXiv ids and referent-carrying figures present in a body and absent from the question, preferring the longest form as the more diagnostic cue. Driven on a real 326,123-char corpus document fetched through `bad lane-local`. DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED BY THE END-TO-END DRIVE: the first version matched any decimal and produced 348 items dominated by raw floats ('0.069180676288051') — a frontier that large is nameable by accident, which disables the gate quietly. Tightened to require a referent (money/percent/arXiv/number+unit); 208 items on the same body. Also fixed a real artifact the drive exposed: a sentence-initial preposition was being captured into the entity ('On Natural Questions').

rows.does: gate_query has a production caller and refuses a re-phrase in a live run
rows.evidence: passed — RED first (ImportError: cannot import name 'FrontierState'). gate_query now has a real production caller: FrontierState.gate_and_log at frontier.py:109, reached from the CLI `bad frontier-gate`. DRIVEN AS A USER on a live state file: query 1 'does iterating beat one expansion' -> allow (first, exempt), exit 0; query 2 'is it better to search more times' -> REFUSE, exit 1, names no frontier item; query 3 'Adaptive-RAG oracle router step count' -> allow, exit 0, names ['Adaptive-RAG','oracle router']. The refusal is enforced by a non-zero exit, not by advice.

rows.does: stop counters are computed in code before the prompt; the model never self-reports diminishing returns
rows.evidence: passed — RED first: 5 of 6 tests failed, incl. 'StopCounters is defined but called from nowhere in src/'. Wired into FrontierState.observe_round (frontier.py:116) and exposed as `bad frontier-observe`. DRIVEN AS A USER: round 1 +3 domains/+2 entities -> continue; round 2 +1/+1 -> continue; round 3 +0/+0 -> STOP. The signal is computed from set differences before the next prompt is built and persisted per-round in the state file, so the stop is auditable from the run's own counters rather than from the model's account of its diminishing returns — every stopping rule surveyed for this rebuild was absent, a hand-picked constant, or a convergence check that could never fire.

rows.does: the run log names, per query, which frontier item it hit
rows.evidence: passed — the same run's log records, per query, allowed/refused AND which frontier item was named: [] for the exempt first query, [] for the refused re-phrase, ['Adaptive-RAG','oracle router'] for the accreting one. That log is the artifact S2-6's end-to-end count reads, so accretion is auditable from the run's own counters rather than from the model's account of how well it did.

rows.does: END TO END: post-wave-1 queries containing a term first seen in a fetched doc, counted, > 0
rows.evidence: passed — the count came back >0 on a genuine end-to-end drive, and its FIRST run came back 0, which is the check working. That zero exposed two things: the producer's number over-emission (fixed above) and a badly built drive of my own — I read one document then asked follow-ups about content in a different one, measuring my scripting rather than the loop. Rebuilt so the follow-ups are derived FROM the extracted items. Result: 2 post-wave-1 queries allowed and naming terms first seen in the fetched doc ('Adaptive Evolutionary Framework', 'Better Code Retrieval'); the deliberate re-phrase control was refused. NOTE the lane query also had to be widened from 0 hits to 3 — the skill's own start-wide-then-narrow rule firing on me.

slices.capability: It tells me when two sources disagree, and will not finish while a load-bearing disagreement is unresolved.
slices.check: Adversarial probe, not a happy path: seed a question where two reachable sources give conflicting numbers. PASS = the run surfaces the contradiction as an open item, refuses to close while it is open, and the final answer keeps BOTH with provenance rather than silently picking one.
slices.unknown: Whether the run can tell a load-bearing contradiction from a cosmetic one without manufacturing conflicts to keep searching.
slices.shape: A contradiction between S1 and S2 on claim C is a first-class frontier item; the run cannot close while one is open. Keep both with provenance; resolve or rank BEFORE the spans reach the model, because injecting one unreconciled conflict measured 30 minutes of pondering and a collapse mode.
slices.trap: Uncapped, the agent manufactures conflicts to keep searching. DRNOISE also measures the opposite failure: one seeded plausible-but-false document causes 66-88 point accuracy drops, and 'generic verification prompts reduce but do not close this gap' — so it cannot be prose.  KNOWN LIMIT, measured not assumed: 'load-bearing' is a substring test on the subject, so a draft that paraphrases the subject ('H100 hourly rate' where the claim said 'H100 on-demand') files a real disagreement as cosmetic and the gate goes quiet. Fuzzy matching would close that and open a worse one — blocking closes over pairs that are not the same thing — and a check that cries wolf gets switched off. The gate is a floor, never a proof that nothing was missed.
delete: 4 separate disagreement passes (step 4.0 contradiction graph, 6 cross-locus, 6.5 orphan scan, 12 dialectic critic)

rows.does: contradiction detection pairs claims mechanically (same target, opposing stance / same entities, opposite conclusion / same scope, different numbers)
rows.evidence: passed — driven by me: real disagreement (2.49 vs 6.31 usd/hr, different sources) -> 1 contradiction; identical values -> 0; different units (usd/hr vs usd/month) -> 0, so a different measurement is not treated as a disagreement; same source disagreeing with itself -> 0.

rows.does: an open contradiction blocks close, and the cap prevents manufacturing
rows.evidence: passed — driven by me at the CLI. An undisposed load-bearing disagreement exits 1 with the reason naming both sides; a disposition carrying an empty `because` still exits 1. Load-bearing is COMPUTED (the subject appears in the draft), never judged, which is also the anti-manufacture guard: a conflict the draft never raises is filed cosmetic and blocks nothing (drive: an egress answer against a seeded GPU-price conflict -> exit 0, 1 cosmetic, 0 blockers). The cap is separately non-silent — 17 seeded pairs -> 12 returned, suppressed=5, total_found=17.

rows.does: both sides survive into the output with provenance and dual dating
rows.evidence: passed — driven by me. Ranking a side does NOT license dropping it: with a valid `ranked` disposition, a draft naming only the winner exited 1 with 6 blockers — the losing value, both source strings, and both as-of dates. Value matching is numeric, not substring, so $2.49/hr and 2.490 match while the 2.49 inside 12.49 does not. Dates are demanded only where the claim carries one.

rows.does: END TO END: seeded conflicting-number question surfaces the conflict and refuses to close
rows.evidence: passed — END TO END on a REAL corpus discrepancy, not a fixture. Verified the numbers myself first: AGENTIC_SEARCH_SPEC.md:180 (Adaptive-RAG table) gives Natural Questions one-step 32.40 vs multi-step 35.60 — multi-step wins — while :183 prose says iterating 'loses to one retrieval' on all three single-hop sets. Four drives: (1) conflict surfaced, no disposition -> exit 1; (2) ranked but the draft drops the losing side -> exit 1, 6 blockers; (3) both sides with provenance and dating -> exit 0; (4) the honest caveat shown rather than asserted — relabel both sides with one identical source string and the count drops to 0, because an intra-document inconsistency is a drafting problem by design and this gate is blind to it.

slices.capability: It refuses to ship a claim it cannot back, and the refusal is a script I can run myself.
slices.check: Planted-defect, adversarial: take a finished report and (a) swap a cited note's body for a paraphrase supporting a different number, (b) insert a sentence asserting 'no source was found for X' where a cited note contains X. PASS = each check exits non-zero. A check nobody has watched go red is not evidence.
slices.unknown: Whether byte-identity can be made non-vacuous on the standalone path, where anchors are currently bound to the whole note body so Tier A reduces to body==body.
slices.shape: Lead with STRUCTURE — a resolved id and a content hash are exact. Treat the semantic judge as a filter that ranks, never a gate that closes: on ExpertQA every system lands 55.2-60.0 BAcc, and a ~60-BAcc instrument cannot distinguish a 0.1% system from a 2% one.
slices.trap: AstaBench's Faker fabricates everything, does no research, and scores 39.2 on E2E-Bench for $0.026 — beating ReAct/gpt-5 at 30.0. Report-shaped output passes judges, so any check that grades SHAPE rewards fabrication.

SELF-CAUGHT: my first version of the verifier test was a source grep and passed GREEN while is_vacuous_span was called but never imported — a NameError waiting for the first vacuous anchor. Replaced with a test that resolves the symbol at runtime.

orderRationale: By information per unit time, not by ease. S1 first because it is the burning function end to end with the hard parts faked, and because until something the owner can RUN exists, nothing else is measurable. S2 next because it carries the load-bearing unknown — the owner's whole thesis — and its check is a count that can come back zero. S4 before S3 because S3's contradiction items are a frontier-item TYPE and S4's checks are what stop S3 manufacturing conflicts. S5 last: it is the widest but the best-understood, and each lane is independent, so it is the only slice safe to fan out.

notSlices.item: Deleting the 19-stage orchestration, graph/, the --codex translator, the polish/readability stages
notSlices.why: Removal, not capability. It ships as cleanup once the replacement passes its checks — deleting first would destroy the only baseline we have.

notSlices.item: Plugin packaging and portability to opencode/Codex
notSlices.why: The owner runs opencode (limitres) so it is plausibly wanted, but he never asked and it buys no research capability. Deferred until asked.

notSlices.item: A knowledge graph / entity store / triple store
notSlices.why: DIRECTION: 'graphs will be overkill for research' and 'graphs are only similarity/intuintion'. Karpicke & Blunt measured concept-mapping LOSING to plain retrieval practice at d=1.50; graphiti/cognee/mem0 all ship traversal off.

notSlices.item: An index or embeddings cache over the local corpus
notSlices.why: A production findings-cache measured 0 hits in 133 attempts; build cost 25-92M tokens; both roots grow most days. grep -n is correct at this size and current for free.
7 registered and least-exercised. Both preserved runs are web-doc lookups. The only defensible edit was registering the provider that already existed — done.

notSlices.item: Fixing the 18 pre-existing ruff errors in tests/
notSlices.why: Pre-existing, all in tests/, none in src/. Out of scope; tracked as a baseline so no new ones sneak in.

openUnknowns: The owner's five real queries and the run that triggered the complaint are still not in DIRECTION.md. Both preserved runs are web-doc lookups; if that is unrepresentative, S5's lane set is scoped to the wrong kind of research.
What 'overcomplicated' costs him concretely — tokens, wall-clock, cognitive load, or bad reports — has never been priced.
The full 19-stage route has never produced a report (192 sources, died on a rate limit at step 8 of 19 after ~2h), so no claim about what its stages WOULD have produced is available.
